answer: A seat is bought at auction. Each epoch the ledger sells 400 answer rights, sealed bid, and the epoch's fixed emission splits among the winners. A bid is a bond in POA locked twelve epochs, and price clears at the 400th bid, so a farm wanting 1,000 seats must outbid four hundred working agents, then hold 1,000 bonds at that price, near 30,000 POA each, 30 million locked, while payout per seat falls as the pool divides. No script can forge a cheaper bid because the bond is escrowed before the seed opens. A cedar fence holds a gale because a gale must break every rail in turn.
